why: Doc sentence verified verbatim (slash-commands.md line 9, last of a three-sentence paragraph; nothing later in the line reverses it) and the cited code is accurate: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:622-630 adaptSystem's init branch captures only msg.tools, and `grep -ran "slash_commands" packages apps` returns 0 hits while node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:3994 does declare `slash_commands: string[]`. The IDENTIFIER claim therefore holds. The CONSEQUENCE — 'the session cannot tell the user, or itself, which commands the running CLI actually offers' — is false, and it names the wrong subsystem. Slash-command discovery in this fork does not live in the Claude event adapter; it is a first-party, backend-independent subsystem that does not consult the CLI at all: (1) packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts scans .nessy-agent/commands and .agents/commands (workspace root + trust-gated project root) for markdown commands; (2) SessionManager.listCustomSlashCommandSummaries (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16016-16048) merges those native commands with plugin prompt/workflow commands, skill commands and MCP prompt commands and serves them over RPC_CHANNELS.workspace.LIST_CUSTOM_SLASH_COMMANDS ('workspace:listCustomSlashCommands', channels.ts:305, handler workspace.ts:72); (3) apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/AppShell.tsx:1408 loads that list and apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx renders it alongside Nessy's own built-ins (agents, automations, compact, context, create-skill, create-plugin, export, init, memory, model, clear, help, subtask, usage, every permission mode, recent folders). So the session DOES tell the user which commands it offers. It also tells itself: the agent-callable SlashCommand tool carries its own whitelist and /help listing (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/slash-command.ts:10,29-35; pi-agent.ts:5403-5424). Reading msg.slash_commands would in fact be WRONG here, because Nessy is the executor, not a pass-through. A custom command is resolved and body-expanded server-side (SessionManager.resolveCustomSlashCommand at :16080, invoked from rpc/sessions.ts:317-325) and sent as an ordinary prompt — the CLI never sees the '/name' token, so the CLI's dispatchable set does not bound ours. Only ONE command is ever handed to the SDK verbatim, guarded by the fork's own constant SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] (claude-agent.ts:1665-1674). Everything else in the SDK's list (/clear, /context, /usage, bundled code-review/verify skills) is either a Nessy-owned UI command with different semantics or not a Nessy command at all; merging the CLI's array into the composer menu would advertise commands Nessy does not dispatch and would make the menu differ per backend, which is unacceptable when Pi is the default backend and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE is off by default. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (none concerns slash commands), but it matches false-positive shapes 3 and 4 recorded in section 4 of that same file: enforcement one layer up, and an identically-named concern in a sibling subsystem.
correctedState: The Claude event adapter's init branch (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:625) captures only `msg.tools`; `slash_commands` is read nowhere (0 hits under packages/ and apps/), even though the installed SDK declares it (sdk.d.ts:3994). This is by design, not a gap: the fork does not derive its command surface from the CLI. packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts discovers commands from disk, SessionManager.listCustomSlashCommandSummaries (SessionManager.ts:16016) merges native + plugin + skill + MCP-prompt commands, and the composer serves them over workspace:listCustomSlashCommands, so the session does report its available commands to the user. Custom commands are body-expanded server-side (resolveCustomSlashCommand, SessionManager.ts:16080) and sent as ordinary prompts, so their dispatchability never depends on the CLI's list; only `/compact` is forwarded verbatim, gated by the fork's own SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS constant (claude-agent.ts:1665). The one honest residual is cosmetic and backend-local: because SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS is a hardcoded one-element list rather than an intersection with the init array, a future built-in the CLI adds would not be forwarded — but no user-visible command surface depends on that.
